questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the road. What can you do?

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the direction they must drive on a one-way street. It is a regulation sign that drivers must obey.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This applies whether the intersection has signs, signals, or neither.

questions.question: If you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, slow down first. This is your most important response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot for other vehicles.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Other vehicles are often hidden in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before you start to change lanes. Signal 100 feet ahead on residential streets or 5 seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead makes a sharp turn. Slow down as if you were making a sharp turn at an intersection.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates. What should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any oncoming train. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Never shift gears while crossing tracks because your vehicle may stall.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process in one hour?
questions.explanation: The average person processes about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, food intake, and your overall health.

questions.question: A small vehicle can start to float in only ____ of water.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded areas. Small vehicles can float in as little as six inches of water. Deeper water can wash a vehicle away.

questions.question: You can cross double solid yellow lines:
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to enter or exit a highway.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line on a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: The most important thing about managing speed in curves is:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down in the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia makes it harder to turn in curves. You must slow down before entering to stay in control.

questions.question: In good driving conditions, keep a following distance of at least:
questions.explanation: In good conditions, keep three to four seconds of distance. On slippery roads, use at least four seconds. In poor conditions, increase your distance.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped with flashing lights, you must stop:
questions.explanation: On all roads and driveways, traffic from both directions must stop before reaching a school bus with red flashing lights.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs give orders that drivers must follow. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Five-sided signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs warn that you are near a school. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down when entering the curve. Speed up when exiting.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up when entering the curve. Slow down when exiting.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when entering the curve. Speed up when exiting.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Then speed up slowly as you exit. If you speed up while entering a curve, your vehicle will be harder to control.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected or hidden road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. They run down the center of the road.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
It does not require drivers to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as mobile crews striping roads, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones use orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the oncoming vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright headlights and helps you see the road so you can stay on course until the other vehicle passes.
